questions: Nothing to match in song 48. The heading, the verse lines and comments m2 to m6 survive only in Tibetan and are themselves the reading text. The only Sanskrit with a Tibetan parallel is cp.48.m1, and all eight of its terms are already matched there with the recorded words: abhasa (snang ba), anguli (sor mo), kaya-vak-citta (lus dang ngag dang yid), mahasukha (bde ba chen po), p-kukkuri (kuk+ku rI pa), p-saraha (sa ra ha), trailokya ('jig rten gsum) and yogi (rnal 'byor pa). So no equivalents are given.

Not in the input's hits, for the reviewer (cp.48.m1): in the Saraha quotation, ghara, 'house', is khyim (khyim ni yod bzhin nags su 'gro bar ma byed cig, 'while you have a house, do not go to the forest'); khyim is already a recorded form of house.

Witness flag, not a term (cp.48.m1): the Tibetan opens with rkang pa bzhi pas 'bras bu'i ngo bo gsungs te / gyen du zhes bya ba la sogs pa, 'with the fourth pada he states the nature of the fruit: "upward" and so on', which the Sanskrit fragment lacks. It renders aṅgulimūrddhīkṛtya, 'raising the finger', literally as sor mo'i steng du byas pa.
